difficulty.reason: Linear's developer platform features a straightforward self-serve OAuth application registration process within user/workspace settings without mandatory upfront reviews for private integrations.

timeEstimate.notes: Applications created in the workspace settings are available immediately for authorization.

requirements.text: Workspace administrator or member privileges to create applications

steps.title: Navigate to Workspace Settings
steps.description: Log into Linear, click on your workspace name in the top left, and navigate to Settings > API & Integrations or Developer settings.

steps.title: Create New OAuth Application
steps.description: Go to the Applications section and click 'New Application' (or 'Create app').

steps.title: Configure App Details and Redirect URIs
steps.description: Provide the application name, description, logo, and your backend's OAuth callback redirect URI(s).

steps.title: Obtain Client ID and Client Secret
steps.description: Save the generated Client ID and Client Secret securely to use in your AI agent backend implementation.

blockers.problem: Redirect URI mismatch errors during authorization code exchange.
blockers.solution: Ensure that the redirect URI sent in the initial authorization request exactly matches character-for-character the redirect URI registered in the Linear application settings.

blockers.problem: Token expiration or missing offline access.
blockers.solution: Ensure proper handling of refresh tokens if the agent needs long-term background access without repeated user re-authentication.

agentCanDo: Construct the authorization URL with required query parameters (client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state)
Handle the OAuth callback code exchange via backend HTTP POST request
Automatically store, encrypt, and refresh access tokens
developerMustDo: Log into the Linear web interface and complete 2FA
Navigate to workspace settings to create the OAuth application and copy credentials
Configure secure environment variables for Client ID and Client Secret

managedOption.managedSufficientWhen: Building multi-tenant AI agents where users connect their own Linear accounts via a managed integration provider like Composio that handles credential storage and token refreshing. Note: This tool was built for a Composio assignment, and Composio sells managed OAuth.
managedOption.customRequiredWhen: Building a tightly-scoped internal enterprise tool or commercial product requiring a branded Linear OAuth client experience and direct control over token storage policies.

claims.claim: Linear allows developers to create OAuth applications directly from workspace settings.
OAuth applications created via workspace settings have instant availability without manual review waits.

openQuestions: What are the exact criteria and process if a developer wants to list their Linear OAuth app publicly in the Linear Integrations Directory?
Are there strict rate limits enforced specifically on custom OAuth client applications?
